newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-SAS Q1 profits seen 45 pct down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-SAS Q1 profits seen 45 pct down.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, May 5 (Reuter) Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) is likely to announce pre-tax profits down 45 percent year-on-year when it publishes 1997 first quarter results on Tuesday, an average of six analysts' forecasts shows.
The analysts on Monday predicted, on average, a profit of 172 million Swedish crowns, compared to 311 million over the first three months of 1996.
The result after financial items was seen falling to 175 million crowns from 244 million, but turnover was seen growing to 8.39 billion crowns from 8.20 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
The analysts said that, despite announcing a cost-cutting programme, SAS still needed to slash outgoings far more.
"It looks at the moment as if cuts have been too little, too late," one forecaster said.
Estimates for first quarter 1997 pre-tax profits ranged from a low of 45 million Swedish crowns to a high of 251 million.
